html:
SMTO-GWT-0026 — Gateway job control unavailable

GUID: 32defd41-2aa3-455a-aa87-65fa628afba6
Slug: gateway-job-control-unavailable
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't reach a background job it started on the Gateway to check on it or control it. The job may still be running, or may have finished, even though this check failed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running the Gateway is switched on and connected, then open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for it. SMTO needs to reach that same Gateway before it can see the job's real status.
  2. Go back to the conversation and look at the Task's progress. If it still shows the job as running, let it keep running. The job may still be working; a failed check does not mean it stopped.
  3. Check whether the job's result already exists, such as the file it was writing or the change it was making, before doing anything else. This tells you whether the job already finished its work, so you don't repeat it.
  4. Only if you're sure the job stopped without doing its work, ask SMTO to run it again. Starting a second copy while the first is still running could make the same change twice or make them clash.

What success looks like

  • The Task shows a final status for the original job (finished, failed or stopped), and the Gateway shows as connected.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway, so they can check the job on that computer. Don't start a replacement job just because SMTO can't reach this one.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway job-control request (inspect, logs, cancel or input) for an existing background job failed, so the job's actual running or completion state is unresolved; the failed observation does not prove the job stopped or failed.

What this means

  • Job control returned a failure to observe or control the recorded job and deliberately omitted a terminal job state. The failed observation cannot establish that the job itself failed. A job-control failure is an observation failure, not proof of termination; conflicting mutation remains unsafe until the original job is reconciled.

Why this can happen

  • Job control returned a failure to observe or control the recorded job and deliberately omitted a terminal job state. The failed observation cannot establish that the job itself failed.

How to diagnose it

  • Keep the recorded job identity and original Gateway; inspect control-runtime availability and any already retained execution receipt.

How to fix it

  • Restore the Server-to-Gateway connection (Check connection; Gateway process and network up), then inspect the original job by its recorded job ID through the same Gateway's job controls. The response carries job_state_unresolved=true and no terminal state; do not start a replacement job, or make a conflicting change, until the original job's state and effects are reconciled.
  • Restore access to the original Gateway job-control runtime through its supported controls. Inspect the existing job by its recorded identity before any conflicting mutation or new launch.

Retry and execution caution

  • Reconcile the original job and its effects before another mutation or replacement launch. Failure to observe a job does not prove that it stopped.

How to verify the fix

  • The original job's state is reconciled through its owning Gateway before conflicting work or replacement launch.

What not to do

  • Do not launch a foreground replacement merely because background job control is unavailable.

Technical notes

  • A job-control failure is an observation failure, not proof of termination; conflicting mutation remains unsafe until the original job is reconciled.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-JOB-0016 — The Gateway couldn't start this background job
  • SMTO-JOB-0001 — SMTO can't tell whether a background job ran
